title: Stoichiometry and Reactions - Chemistry - Balancing Equations
subject: Chemistry

questions.q: Why must chemical equations be balanced?
options: To ensure the reaction proceeds quickly
To satisfy the Law of Conservation of Mass
To determine the limiting reagent immediately
To change the chemical properties of products
questions.explain: Chemical equations must be balanced to satisfy the Law of Conservation of Mass, which states that matter cannot be created or destroyed.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q:
What is the correct coefficient for O$_2$ when the following equation is balanced?
CH$_4$ + __O$_2$ ​$\rightarrow$ CO$_2$ + H$_2$O
questions.explain: Balanced equation: $\text{CH}_4 + 2\text{O}_2 \rightarrow \text{CO}_2 + 2\text{H}_2\text{O}$. The coefficient for Oxygen is 2.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: When the equation Fe + O$_2$ ​$\rightarrow$ Fe$_2$O​$_3$ is balanced with the lowest whole number coefficients, what is the coefficient of Fe?
questions.explain: Balanced equation: $4\text{Fe} + 3\text{O}_2 \rightarrow 2\text{Fe}_2\text{O}_3$. The coefficient for Fe is 4.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: Balance the following equation: Al + Cl$_2$ ​$\rightarrow$ AlCl$_3$. What are the coefficients?
questions.explain: We need 3 Cl$_2$ to get 6 Cl atoms, and 2 AlCl$_3$ to match. Thus: $2\text{Al} + 3\text{Cl}_2 \rightarrow 2\text{AlCl}_3$.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q:
What is the sum of all coefficients when the following equation is balanced using lowest whole numbers?
C$_3$H​$_8$ + O$_2$ ​$\rightarrow$ CO$_2$ + H$_2$O
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.explain: Two nitrogens on left require 2 NH$_3$. This gives 6 hydrogens, requiring 3 H$_2$.

questions.q: In the reaction $2\text{KClO}_3 \rightarrow 2\text{KCl} + 3\text{O}_2$, how many atoms of Oxygen are on the reactant side?

questions.q: Identify the missing coefficient (x) in: P$_4$ + xO$_2$ ​$\rightarrow$ P$_4$O​$_{10}$
questions.explain: We need 10 oxygen atoms on the left. Since O$_2$ has 2, x must be 5 ($5 \times 2 = 10$).
